liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Cat Sunflower** (2 reviews): Reviewer says the China Cat into Rider pairing will stay with them forever; Reviewer finds the China Cat into Rider sweet [21][27]
- **To Lay Me Down** (1 review): To Lay Me Down in the acoustic set won this reviewer over [21]
- **Ripple** (1 review): Reviewer got chills from the harmonies on Ripple [27]
- **Little Red Rooster (2)** (1 other source): Matt Kelly sat in on Little Red Rooster [1]
- **Deal** (1 review): Reviewer says this Deal really comes together [22]
- **Fire On The Mountain (3)** (1 other source): John Cippolina guested on Fire On The Mountain, and also Wharf Rat, Around & Around and Sunshine Daydream [1]
- **Satisfaction** (1 review): Reviewer hears a strong encore Satisfaction, followed by a nice Brokedown Palace [20]

## Setlist highlights

- **Thank You Uncle Bobo!**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]
- **New Years Countdown**: rare: 9 archived performances [30]
- **Jerry w/Drums**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]
- **I Can't Get No (Satisfaction)**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [30]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-12-31.mtx.tobin.105029.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 36 songs; 246 min; rated 3.8/5 by 5 [1]
- **gd1980-12-31.155390.PandP-sbd.gems-tobin.flac16**: soundboard; 36 songs; 228 min [6]
- **gd80-12-31.rolfe.vernon.16911.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 34 songs; 247 min; rated 3/5 by 3 [11]. Said about its sound: Audience recording picks up loud crowd noise early on; the crowd is quieter by the third set; Audience recording sounds distant, lacking clarity and presence, though the full frequency range is present [20][23]
- **gd80-12-31.sbd.gorinsky.6391.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 30 songs; 219 min; rated 3.75/5 by 16 [15]. Said about its sound: Soundboard has dropouts and a stretch that seems to be swapped in from an audience tape; Soundboard has a warm, slightly fuzzy sound that feels good [22][25]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says the hall was a poor place to play acoustic music [18]
- The Dinosaurs opened the night; the reviewer only learned this on arrival [19]
- After the double encore, Bobby tells the crowd, without much energy, that Bill Graham will serve breakfast shortly [20]
- Reviewer stood up front on the floor for the acoustic set and surrendered the whole ticket to enter [21]
- The party mood began in the acoustic set, building steadily in pace [22]
- By the end of the final acoustic set, the whole auditorium was surging, clapping and singing along [33]
- Reviewer says most New Year's Eve shows disappointed; '76, '78 and '82 were exceptions [19]
- Reviewer notes the band's playing had evolved since the Warfield and Radio City runs [24]
- Reviewer knows of no other show where they played Satisfaction [28]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-12-31.mtx.tobin.105029.flac16**: transferred by Kevin Tobin; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [1]
- **gd1980-12-31.155390.PandP-sbd.gems-tobin.flac16**: transferred by Patched and pitch corrected Soundboard by Kevin Tobin; source: Patched and pitch corrected Soundboard [6]. Also: Mixed from the GEMs soundboard, patched with parts from other sources like a jigsaw puzzle; GEMs soundboard runs fast, about 1.2 seconds per minute; some dead air was trimmed for a video project [6]
- **gd80-12-31.rolfe.vernon.16911.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Steve Rolfe; source: Audience Recording: Nak 300 Shotguns [11]
- **gd80-12-31.sbd.gorinsky.6391.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [15]
